solution:
Use integration by parts with $u=x^{2}$, $dv=e^{x}dx$ (so $du=2x\,dx$, $v=e^{x}$):
$$\int x^{2}e^{x}\,dx=x^{2}e^{x}-\int2xe^{x}\,dx.$$
For $\int2xe^{x}\,dx$, apply parts again with $u=2x$, $dv=e^{x}dx$:
$$\int2xe^{x}\,dx=2xe^{x}-\int2e^{x}\,dx=2xe^{x}-2e^{x}.$$
Therefore
$$\int x^{2}e^{x}\,dx=x^{2}e^{x}-2xe^{x}+2e^{x}+C=e^{x}(x^{2}-2x+2)+C.$$
hints: Let u = x^2 so the power reduces on differentiating.
